assessment: In this interesting study, the authors provide important insights into how titin derived from different nuclei within the syncytium is organized and integrated after cell fusion during skeletal muscle development and remodeling. This solid work elucidates the intricate process of myofilament assembly and disassembly, made possible by tracking labeled sarcomere components. The authors developed a novel mCherry titin knock-in mice with the fluorophore mCherry inserted into titin's Z-disk region to track the titin during cell fusion. The findings of the study could be important for developing therapeutic targets for diseases associated with skeletal muscle.
